title: NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException for an interface with two implementations: annotate the interface with @Primary
errorSample:
Caused by: org.springframework.beans.factory.NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException: No qualifying bean of type 'task.PaymentGateway' available: expected single matching bean but found 2: bankTransferGateway,cardPaymentGateway
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.config.DependencyDescriptor.resolveNotUnique(DependencyDescriptor.java:192) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.DefaultListableBeanFactory.doResolveDependency(DefaultListableBeanFactory.java:1746) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.DefaultListableBeanFactory.resolveDependency(DefaultListableBeanFactory.java:1658) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.ConstructorResolver.resolveAutowiredArgument(ConstructorResolver.java:912) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	at org.springframework.beans.factory.support.ConstructorResolver.createArgumentArray(ConstructorResolver.java:791) ~[spring-beans-7.0.9.jar:7.0.9]
	... 122 common frames omitted
symptom: Startup fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException: expected single matching bean but found 2, for a constructor parameter typed with an interface that has two component implementations.
cause: Both implementations register as candidates for the interface type and nothing marks one of them as the default choice.
fixSummary: Mark the shared interface with @Primary. Because both implementations are assignable to it, Spring treats the interface-level marker as the default selection and injects the candidate it describes without touching the implementations or the injection point.
